# Heatmap

A grid of cells tinted by value, for activity by hour, a year of days or a retention cohort. Scale it per grid, row or column; every cell reads out on hover, on focus and to screen readers.

```tsx
<Heatmap
  data={traffic}
  rows={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
  columns={hours}
  label="Visits by weekday and hour"
  valueFormatter={(value) => `${value} visits`}
>
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels interval={3} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
  <HeatmapLegend />
</Heatmap>
```

## Installation

```bash
# One-time setup (tokens + lib helpers)
npx koalaui-cli@latest init

# Add this component (its dependencies come along)
npx koalaui-cli@latest add heatmap
```

Manual: run `npm install tailwind-variants tailwind-merge tippy.js`, then copy the source into `components/ui/heatmap/` and adjust the import paths to your project. Components pull `cn` from `lib/utils`, the `tv` wrapper from `lib/tv`, and (for multi-part components) `createContext` from `lib/create-context`.

## Usage

`Heatmap` is composed from named parts, like [Chart](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/chart.md). The root takes the `data` (one array per row), the `rows` and `columns` labels and the colour scale. `HeatmapGrid` draws the cells; `HeatmapRowLabels` and `HeatmapColumnLabels` go inside it so they line up with the cells, and `HeatmapLegend` is the Less / More key.

```tsx title="traffic-heatmap.tsx"
import {
  Heatmap,
  HeatmapGrid,
  HeatmapRowLabels,
  HeatmapColumnLabels,
  HeatmapLegend,
} from "@/components/ui/heatmap"

const days = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
const hours = Array.from({ length: 24 }, (_, h) => `${h % 12 || 12}${h < 12 ? "am" : "pm"}`)

// traffic: 7 rows (days) of 24 numbers (hours)
export function TrafficHeatmap({ traffic }: { traffic: number[][] }) {
  return (
    <Heatmap data={traffic} rows={days} columns={hours} label="Visits by weekday and hour">
      <HeatmapGrid>
        <HeatmapRowLabels />
        <HeatmapColumnLabels interval={3} />
      </HeatmapGrid>
      <HeatmapLegend />
    </Heatmap>
  )
}
```

## Activity card

The dashboard widget: one row per event, one column per day, in a [Card](https://koala-ui.vercel.app/docs/components/card.md). Visits and abandonments are a thousand times apart, so each row is shaded against itself (`normalize="row"`), and the tooltip adds the date the column header leaves out through `renderTooltip`. Switch the week: the cells tween to their new shades instead of redrawing.

```tsx
const [week, setWeek] = React.useState<WeekKey>("current")
const data = ACTIVITY[week]

<Card className="w-full max-w-md">
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>User activity</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription className="tabular-nums">{total.toLocaleString("en-US")} events</CardDescription>
    <CardAction>
      <Select value={week} onValueChange={(value) => setWeek(value as WeekKey)}>
        <SelectTrigger size="sm" aria-label="Activity week" className="w-32">
          <SelectValue />
        </SelectTrigger>
        <SelectContent>
          <SelectItem value="current">This week</SelectItem>
          <SelectItem value="previous">Last week</SelectItem>
        </SelectContent>
      </Select>
    </CardAction>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    <Heatmap
      data={data.rows.map((row) => row.counts)}
      rows={data.rows.map((row) => row.event)}
      columns={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
      normalize="row"
      color="brand"
      label={`Events per day, ${data.dates[0]} to ${data.dates[6]}`}
    >
      <HeatmapGrid
        renderTooltip={(cell) => (
          <TooltipHeader>
            <TooltipHeaderText>
              <TooltipTitle>{cell.rowLabel}</TooltipTitle>
              <TooltipDescription>
                {cell.columnLabel}, {data.dates[cell.column]}
              </TooltipDescription>
            </TooltipHeaderText>
            <TooltipValue>{cell.formattedValue}</TooltipValue>
          </TooltipHeader>
        )}
      >
        <HeatmapRowLabels />
        <HeatmapColumnLabels />
      </HeatmapGrid>
      <HeatmapLegend />
    </Heatmap>
  </CardContent>
</Card>
```

## Normalization

`normalize` decides what a cell’s shade is measured against. `grid` (the default) puts every cell on one scale, the honest reading when the rows share a unit and a magnitude. `row` shades each row from its own quietest cell to its busiest, for rows that differ by orders of magnitude; `column` does the same down each column. The tooltip and each cell’s accessible name always carry the real number, whatever the shade.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="grid" aspect="wide">…</Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" aspect="wide">…</Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="column" aspect="wide">…</Heatmap>

// each one:
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" aspect="wide" label="Events per day, normalised by row">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>
```

## Calendar strip

A year of days, one column per week. `size="sm"` tightens the gaps and lowers the cell minimum, so 53 weeks fit a card; on a phone the strip scrolls sideways inside its own box while the day labels stay pinned. `null` marks the days before the range starts (a blank, not a zero). `tickFormatter` prints each month once and every other weekday, and `cellLabel` names each cell by its real date. The legend is a part like any other, so it can share a row with a summary.

```tsx
// deploys: 7 rows (Mon to Sun) of 53 weeks; null before the range starts.
// dayAt(row, column) turns a cell back into its date.
<Heatmap
  data={deploys}
  rows={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
  columns={weekLabels}
  size="sm"
  color="teal"
  label="Deploys per day, last 12 months"
  valueFormatter={(value) => `${value} ${value === 1 ? "deploy" : "deploys"}`}
>
  <HeatmapGrid
    cellLabel={(cell) => `${cell.formattedValue} on ${longDate.format(dayAt(cell.row, cell.column))}`}
    renderTooltip={(cell) => (
      <TooltipHeader>
        <TooltipHeaderText>
          <TooltipTitle>{cell.formattedValue}</TooltipTitle>
          <TooltipDescription>{longDate.format(dayAt(cell.row, cell.column))}</TooltipDescription>
        </TooltipHeaderText>
      </TooltipHeader>
    )}
  >
    <HeatmapRowLabels tickFormatter={(label, index) => (index % 2 === 0 && index < 6 ? label : null)} />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels tickFormatter={monthTick} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
  <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-x-4 gap-y-2">
    <p className="text-sm text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{total.toLocaleString("en-US")} deploys in the last year</p>
    <HeatmapLegend />
  </div>
</Heatmap>

/** A month's name over the first week that opens in it (not in the last two, where it would not fit). */
function monthTick(_label: string, week: number) {
  if (week > WEEKS - 3) return null
  const month = dayAt(0, week).getUTCMonth()
  return week === 0 || month !== dayAt(0, week - 1).getUTCMonth() ? monthName.format(dayAt(0, week)) : null
}
```

## Retention cohort

The share of each signup cohort still active week by week. Newer cohorts have lived fewer weeks, so the weeks still to come are `null` and the grid reads as a triangle. `domain={[0, 100]}` pins the scale to the whole percentage range instead of the data’s own, so a cell’s shade means the same thing in every report, and `steps={6}` gives the scale more shades to tell the weeks apart.

```tsx
// retention: one row per cohort, one column per week; the weeks still to come are null.
<Heatmap
  data={retention}
  rows={["Jul 27", "Aug 3", "Aug 10", "Aug 17", "Aug 24", "Aug 31", "Sep 7", "Sep 14"]}
  columns={["Week 0", "Week 1", "Week 2", "Week 3", "Week 4", "Week 5", "Week 6", "Week 7"]}
  domain={[0, 100]}
  steps={6}
  color="purple"
  label="Weekly retention by signup cohort"
  valueFormatter={(value) => `${value}%`}
  className="w-full max-w-xl"
>
  <HeatmapGrid
    cellLabel={(cell) => `${cell.rowLabel} cohort, ${cell.columnLabel}: ${cell.formattedValue} retained`}
    renderTooltip={(cell) => (
      <TooltipHeader>
        <TooltipHeaderText>
          <TooltipTitle>{cell.rowLabel} cohort</TooltipTitle>
          <TooltipDescription>{cell.columnLabel}</TooltipDescription>
        </TooltipHeaderText>
        <TooltipValue>{cell.formattedValue}</TooltipValue>
      </TooltipHeader>
    )}
  >
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels tickFormatter={(label) => label.replace("Week ", "W")} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
  <HeatmapLegend lowLabel="0%" highLabel="100%" />
</Heatmap>
```

## Colors

The scale is one hue mixed into the muted track: an empty cell is the track itself and each step adds more of the hue until the last is the hue at full strength. The hues are the Chart’s: `blue` (the default, the house chart hue), `brand` for a heatmap that is the story of the screen, `primary`, the accents, the status roles, and `current` to build the scale from the ambient text colour. Every hue re-themes across light, dark, cream and moonlight.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="blue" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="brand" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="primary" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="purple" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="pink" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="teal" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="orange" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="success" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="warning" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="info" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="destructive" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>

// current: the scale takes the ambient text colour
<div className="text-foreground">
  <Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} color="current" size="sm"><HeatmapGrid /></Heatmap>
</div>
```

## Steps

`steps` sets how many shades sit above the empty track (four by default, up to ten). Fewer steps read faster and hide small differences; more steps show them. The legend always paints the scale the grid uses.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} steps={3} size="sm">
  <HeatmapGrid />
  <HeatmapLegend />
</Heatmap>

<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} size="sm">{/* 4, the default */}…</Heatmap>
<Heatmap data={visits} rows={days} columns={hours} steps={7} size="sm">…</Heatmap>
```

## Size

Cells always share the width of the box, down to a minimum. `md` (the default) keeps them at least 24px with 4px gaps, room for a three-letter label over every column in a dashboard card; `sm` goes down to 10px with 2px gaps, for a dense strip. Below the minimum the grid scrolls sideways inside its own box, never the page.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={traffic} rows={days} columns={hours} size="md">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels interval={3} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>

<Heatmap data={traffic} rows={days} columns={hours} size="sm">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels interval={3} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>
```

## Aspect

Cells are square by default, so a many-column grid keeps its proportions. `aspect="wide"` holds one row height (28px at `md`, 12px at `sm`) and lets the cells stretch across their column, for a few columns in a lot of width, where squares would make a tower.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" color="brand" className="max-w-sm">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>

<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" color="brand" aspect="wide">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>
```

## Only the parts you need

Every part is optional. Leave out the legend for a tight card, or the labels too for a bare strip beside a figure: the grid takes back the room they would have used, with no gutter left behind. The tooltip is a render prop on `HeatmapGrid`; return `null` to go without one.

```tsx
// Legend dropped
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" aspect="wide">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>

// Labels and legend dropped: a bare strip
<Heatmap data={weekdayTraffic} rows={days} columns={hours} size="sm">
  <HeatmapGrid />
</Heatmap>

// Tooltips dropped: renderTooltip returns null
<Heatmap data={counts} rows={events} columns={days} normalize="row" aspect="wide">
  <HeatmapGrid renderTooltip={() => null}>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
  <HeatmapLegend />
</Heatmap>
```

## Load animation

Like the Chart, a heatmap plays a one-shot reveal when it mounts: the cells fade and grow in a diagonal wave from the top-left corner. It never replays on hover or when the data changes (a changed cell tweens its shade instead), and it holds still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. Pass `animate={false}` to opt out. Press Replay to watch it again.

```tsx
// On by default. Bump a key to replay it; pass animate={false} to opt out.
<Heatmap key={run} data={traffic} rows={days} columns={hours} label="Visits by weekday and hour">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels interval={3} />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>
```

## Empty state

With no rows or no columns, `HeatmapGrid` shows a muted message in place of the cells and the labels and legend step aside. Pass `empty` on the root to say something more useful. A grid of zeros is not empty: it paints the muted track, which is the truth.

```tsx
<Heatmap data={[]} label="Visits by weekday and hour">
  <HeatmapGrid>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
  <HeatmapLegend />
</Heatmap>

<Heatmap data={[]} label="Deploys per day" empty="No deploys in this period yet">
  …
</Heatmap>
```

## Accessibility

The cells are an ARIA grid named by `label`. It is one tab stop: the arrow keys move between cells (skipping blanks), Home and End jump to the ends of a row, and Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the first and last cell. Focus opens the same tooltip as hover. Every cell carries its full reading as its name (“Sign-ups, Mon: 131”), so the row and column labels are decorative duplicates hidden from assistive tech, and the legend is too. Write a `cellLabel` when the labels alone do not say what a cell is, like a calendar day.

```tsx title="accessible-heatmap.tsx"
<Heatmap
  data={deploys}
  rows={days}
  columns={weeks}
  // The grid's accessible name.
  label="Deploys per day, last 12 months"
  valueFormatter={(value) => `${value} deploys`}
>
  {/* Each cell's name. The default is "row, column: value". */}
  <HeatmapGrid cellLabel={(cell) => `${cell.formattedValue} on ${dateOf(cell)}`}>
    <HeatmapRowLabels />
    <HeatmapColumnLabels />
  </HeatmapGrid>
</Heatmap>
```

## API reference

`Heatmap` takes `data` (an array of rows, each an array of `number | null`), `rows` and `columns` (the labels), `normalize` (`grid | row | column`), `domain` (a fixed `[low, high]`), `steps` (default 4), `color` (default `blue`), `size` (`sm | md`), `aspect` (`square | wide`), `valueFormatter`, `label` (the grid’s accessible name), `animate` (the load reveal, on by default) and `empty`, and forwards `div` props. `HeatmapGrid` takes `renderTooltip` and `cellLabel`, both called with the cell (`row`, `column`, `rowLabel`, `columnLabel`, `value`, `formattedValue`, `level`). `HeatmapRowLabels` and `HeatmapColumnLabels` take `tickFormatter` and `interval`, like the Chart’s axes; `HeatmapLegend` takes `lowLabel` and `highLabel`. Every part accepts `className`, merged last, and carries a `data-slot`; cells also carry `data-row`, `data-column` and `data-level`.

## FAQ

### What shape does data take?

One array per row, one entry per column: data={[[4, 0, 12], [7, 3, 9]]}. Pass rows and columns with the labels in the same order. Ragged rows are padded with blanks, and anything that is not a finite number becomes a blank cell.

### What is the difference between 0 and null?

Zero is a real reading of nothing: the cell paints the muted track and still has a tooltip and a name. null is no reading at all: the cell stays blank, takes no focus and has no tooltip, which is how the days before a calendar starts or the future weeks of a retention cohort should look.

### When should I normalise per row?

When the rows measure different things at very different magnitudes, like visits and refunds. On one shared scale the small rows would all sit on the lightest step. With normalize="row" each row is shaded from its own quietest cell to its busiest, so its shape reads; the numbers in the tooltip stay exact. Say so in the label, since shades are then not comparable across rows.

### How do I pin the scale to a known range?

Pass domain={[low, high]}, for example [0, 100] for percentages. Every cell is then measured against that range, so a shade means the same in every report and normalize no longer applies.

### Why does the colour look lighter than the hue?

The scale mixes the hue into the muted track: the first step is mostly track and the last step is the hue itself. That keeps an empty cell and the lightest step apart in every theme, including the dark ones, where a translucent tint over the card would sink into it.

### How do I change what the tooltip shows?

Pass renderTooltip to HeatmapGrid. It receives the cell (labels, value, formatted value, level) and returns the tooltip body, composed from the Tooltip graph parts. Return null for a cell to give it no tooltip.

### How do I show only some labels?

HeatmapRowLabels and HeatmapColumnLabels take interval (every Nth label) and tickFormatter (return a label, or null to leave that slot empty), the same props as the Chart's axes. Labels never widen a column, so every column stays the same width. A label followed by an empty slot is a tick: it marks its column from the start edge and spills over the empty slots, the way month names sit over a year of weeks. Labelled neighbours sit centred, so keep those short (Mon, 9am) or thin them out.

### What happens on a phone?

Cells never shrink below the size minimum (24px at md, 10px at sm). When the columns cannot fit, the grid scrolls sideways inside its own box and the row labels stay pinned to the start edge, so the page itself never overflows.

### Is it accessible to keyboard and screen reader users?

Yes. The cells form an ARIA grid with one tab stop and arrow key navigation, and focus opens the tooltip. Every cell's accessible name is its full reading, so a screen reader announces "Sign-ups, Mon: 131" rather than a colour. Name the grid with label.

### Can I turn off the load animation?

Pass animate={false} on Heatmap. The reveal plays once on mount, never on hover or data changes, and it is held still under prefers-reduced-motion.

## Exports and dependencies

`npx koalaui-cli@latest add heatmap` writes `components/ui/heatmap/`. Import from `@/components/ui/heatmap`:

- Components and helpers: `Heatmap`, `HeatmapGrid`, `HeatmapRowLabels`, `HeatmapColumnLabels`, `HeatmapLegend`, `heatmapVariants`
- Types: `HeatmapProps`, `HeatmapGridProps`, `HeatmapLabelsProps`, `HeatmapLegendProps`, `HeatmapCell`, `HeatmapColor`, `HeatmapNormalize`
- Koala components it installs with it: `tooltip`
- Koala lib helpers it uses: `create-context`, `motion`, `tv`
